references.text: The Jews demanded a sign from Jesus as proof of his authority, showing the same pattern of demanding signs to believe: [ref:Joh 2:18|John 2:18].
The crowd asked Jesus for a sign so that they might believe in him, even though they had already seen his miracles: [ref:Joh 6:30|John 6:30].
Jesus tells Thomas that those who believe without seeing are blessed – contrasting with those who demand signs and wonders to believe: [ref:Joh 20:29|John 20:29].
Paul writes that the Jews demand signs, reflecting the attitude Jesus rebukes here: [ref:1 Kor 1:22|1 Corinthians 1:22].
The scribes and Pharisees asked Jesus for a sign, and he called them an evil and adulterous generation seeking a sign: [ref:Matt 12:38-39|Matthew 12:38-39].
The Pharisees and Sadducees tested Jesus by asking for a sign from heaven, and Jesus rejected their demand: [ref:Matt 16:1-4|Matthew 16:1-4].
The Pharisees demanded a sign from heaven, and Jesus sighed deeply in his spirit and asked why this generation demands signs: [ref:Mark 8:11-12|Mark 8:11-12].
The official believed Jesus' word without first seeing the sign – contrasting with the rebuke in verse 48, showing obedient faith: [ref:Joh 4:50|John 4:50].
Jesus called that generation an evil generation demanding a sign, paralleling his rebuke of the demand for signs: [ref:Luk 11:29|Luke 11:29].
